provenance.note: Status changes only with a dated citation; per-commitment citations inline (commitment_source + status_history entries). sources_note names the verification calendar (Climate Budget commissioning table, ESR works chapters, NGT record, RTI manuals, MMRDA status pages) - which is why those registry entries carry this file in dependsOn.

headline: 19 commitments on Mumbai's register: 5 on track, 4 rescheduled with a new date, 2 stalled, and 8 whose current status we cannot yet cite either way.
intro: Dated commitments by the institutions that manage this city's water - BMC, MMRDA, the state government and the tribunals that set deadlines for them - made to residents, courts and funders, and followed from announcement to delivery. Every commitment carries its original citation and every status change carries a dated source. Delivered late is still delivered - the dates show the journey - and when a date moves, the old one stays on the record. Nothing here is our opinion; it is the institutions' own paper, checked against time.

status_legend.delivered: Done, with a source confirming it
status_legend.slipped: Officially or credibly re-dated - the old and new dates are both kept
status_legend.overdue: Past its promised date with no official word
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

commitments.title: Versova WWTF - 180 MLD next-generation plant
commitments.what: Replacement sewage plant at Versova, part of the 7-plant, 2,464 MLD upgrade with 50% tertiary reuse. The existing plant has failed the discharge standard for years (outlet BOD 58 mg/l in 2024).

commitment_source.label: BMC's own documents, twice over: Climate Budget Report 2025-26 (commissioning dates) AND ESR 2024-25 Table 11.1 (expected completion 04.07.2026)

status_history.note: BMC's own ESR Table 11.1 records the plant at 24.80% physical completion on 30.04.2025 - fourteen months before its own printed completion date
Press reported ~32% with a year to go
BMC now targets all seven plants by July 2027; the printed 04-07-2026 date passed unmet

BMC's Additional Municipal Commissioner (Projects) said 'around 80% of the project work had been completed' at the Versova plant, and the report says its structural work has been completed. The Versova and Ghatkopar plants 'are expected to be completed by March 31, 2027'. The plant's date is now 31 March 2027, against 04.07.2026 in the ESR; the new date has not passed.
status_history.source_label: Free Press Journal, reporting BMC's Additional Municipal Commissioner (Projects), 14 October 2026

commitments.title: Ghatkopar WWTF - 337 MLD next-generation plant
commitments.what: Replacement plant at Ghatkopar, discharging toward Thane Creek; the existing works fail the standard (outlet BOD 24.5 mg/l in 2024).

commitment_source.label: Climate Budget Report 2025-26 AND ESR 2024-25 Table 11.1 (expected completion 04.07.2026)

status_history.note: BMC's own ESR Table 11.1: 40.00% physical completion on 30.04.2025
Re-dated to ~July 2027 with the rest of the programme

BMC has set 'a December 31, 2026 deadline for completing the liquid pipeline' needed for secondary treatment, and 'the entire project is targeted for completion by March 31, 2027'; the site workforce was reported increased to about 1,000 from the first week of October. The report gives no percentage of work done. The plant's date is now 31 March 2027, against 04.07.2026 in the ESR; the new date has not passed.
status_history.source_label: Free Press Journal, reporting BMC and its Additional Municipal Commissioner (Projects), 8 October 2026

commitments.title: Bhandup WWTF - 215 MLD next-generation plant
commitments.what: Replacement plant at Bhandup; the most advanced of the seven (51% in July 2025).

commitment_source.label: Climate Budget Report 2025-26 AND ESR 2024-25 Table 11.1 (expected completion 22.08.2026)

status_history.note: BMC's own ESR Table 11.1: 43.07% on 30.04.2025 - the most advanced of the seven
Now directed to be fully operational by October 2026 ('final stage of construction'; commissioner-level push reported)

commitments.title: The full 7-plant programme: 2,464 MLD treated, 1,233 MLD recycled
commitments.what: Worli 500 + Malad 454 + Dharavi 418 + Bandra 360 + Ghatkopar 337 + Bhandup 215 + Versova 180 MLD, with 1,233 MLD tertiary reuse - quietly the biggest 'new water source' in the region's pipeline. BMC's own ESR (30.04.2025) put overall physical progress at 25-43% per plant; the ESR's own completion dates are 2026 (three plants), 2027 (three) and 2028 (Malad).

commitment_source.label: BMC via FPJ: '1,233 MLD recycled water by end of 2027'; ESR 2024-25 Table 11.1 carries per-plant % complete

status_history.note: ESR Table 11.1 per-plant completion: Worli 29.02%, Bandra 33.12%, Dharavi 30.08%, Versova 24.80%, Malad 24.91%, Bhandup 43.07%, Ghatkopar 40.00%
BMC says all seven by July 2027 with 1,233 MLD by end-2027 - though usable tertiary water is expected only from Oct-Nov 2027 (monsoon dilution), and the ESR's own Malad date is 2028

commitments.title: Powai Lake 8 MLD STP
commitments.what: The 8 MLD plant at the defunct Powai sewage pumping station, part of the response to the ~18 MLD of sewage the NGT record describes entering Powai Lake. BMC's affidavit before the NGT put its commissioning no earlier than 11 December 2027; in September 2026 BMC said it had diverted the lake's sewage outflows to the Bhandup and Filterpada plants and targets the STP by May 2027.

commitment_source.label: NGT OA 150/2025 proceedings (commissioning not before 11 Dec 2027)

status_history.note: A rejoinder before the NGT (Western Zone, Original Application No. 150 of 2025) responds to BMC's affidavit, under whose timeline the proposed 8 MLD STP at the Powai pumping station 'will not be commissioned until 11 December 2027'. The report gives no progress figure for the plant, so its status cannot be cited either way.
status_history.source_label: Free Press Journal, reporting BMC's affidavit before the NGT, 7 June 2026

status_history.note: BMC said it plans to start the 8 MLD STP 'by May 2027'; the plant 'is being constructed at the defunct sewage pumping station in Powai'. BMC reported 20 sewage outflows intercepted and diverted to the Bhandup and Filterpada STPs, with 3,056 metres of new sewer lines laid, and planned to stop sewage entering the lake from 1 October. No progress figure is given for the STP itself.
status_history.source_label: Free Press Journal, reporting BMC (with BMC's post on X), 30 September 2026

commitments.title: Demolish the illegal Aksa beach promenade
commitments.what: The NGT ordered the Rs 11.8 cr promenade demolished within two months as a CRZ violation, after it obstructed tidal flows and partly collapsed into the sea.

status_history.note: The two-month deadline passed in November 2025; no public confirmation of demolition (or of a stay) found - awaiting a citable update
status_history.source_label: Neer Vazhvu verification pass, against the NGT judgment of 16 September 2025 as reported by Free Press Journal

commitments.title: New 2,000 MLD Bhandup water treatment plant
commitments.what: Design-build-operate replacement for the 1981 plant that was once Asia's largest - the single biggest treatment commitment in the city's history.

commitment_source.label: Free Press Journal, 30 Jan 2026: the new 2,000 MLD plant is 'scheduled for completion by April 2029'

status_history.note: The new 2,000 MLD plant is 'scheduled for completion by April 2029'. A senior civic official said 'work has accelerated on soil testing, excavation, site barricading, relocation of power lines'. No progress figure is given, so the status cannot be cited either way.
status_history.source_label: Free Press Journal, reporting a senior BMC official, 30 January 2026

status_history.note: BMC lists 'A 2000 MLD WTP at Bhandup Complex, along with a 2000 MLD Clear Water Pumping Station' among the treatment-plant works 'being carried out', to replace the existing 1910 MLD plant. No progress figure is given.
status_history.source_label: BMC, Climate Budget Report FY 2026-27 (Water Supply Projects Department)

commitments.title: Panjrapur +910 MLD advanced treatment unit
commitments.what: Takes the Pise-Panjrapur works from 1,365 to 1,820 MLD (~4-year build).

status_history.note: Welspun Enterprises Limited is to build the unit; 'The total project cost is estimated to be Rs 3,145 crore', the upgrade will 'raise the plant's total capacity from 1,365 MLD to 1,820 MLD', and the work is 'expected to be completed over the next four years'. No progress figure is given.
BMC lists 'a 910 MLD WTP at Panjrapur to treat raw water by replacing two compartments of existing WTP' among the treatment-plant works 'being carried out'. No progress figure is given.
status_history.source_label: BMC, Climate Budget Report FY 2026-27 (Water Supply Projects Department)

commitments.title: Gargai dam: +440 MLD - approved 2013, tendered 2025
commitments.what: Mumbai's first new source since 2014. The Rs 3,000 cr tender finally floated in December 2025, twelve years after approval; would submerge ~2,100 acres of Tansa sanctuary forest and displace 619 tribal families. Staging says 2026-2030.

commitment_source.label: BMC staging (FPJ Sept 2025); displacement record at Land Conflict Watch

status_history.note: Project first approved - the clock starts here
Tender floated after a twelve-year pause; 2030 target set

commitments.title: Manori desalination: 200 MLD (expandable to 400)
commitments.what: Mumbai's first desalination plant. Staging said 2025-2029; the DPR is done and tendering 'in progress' per the WSP department's own RTI manual (Dec 2024).

commitment_source.label: BMC WSP RTI manual (Dec 2024) + expansion staging (FPJ)

status_history.note: 'Mumbai is developing a 200 MLD desalination plant at Manori and Versova in the Western suburbs.' The report gives no tender or progress status.
status_history.source_label: Free Press Journal, on BMC's water-supply expansion plans, 27 September 2025

status_history.note: BMC's Additional Municipal Commissioner (Projects) said: 'All necessary permissions have been received. The full-fledged work on ground will start post-monsoon', and that the plant 'will produce 200 MLD by 2029'. The report records MCZMA approval on 7 April and the Union environment ministry's final CRZ clearance on 28 April 2026. With on-ground work to start after the monsoon, there is no progress figure for the plant.
status_history.source_label: ThePrint, reporting BMC's Additional Municipal Commissioner (Projects), 28 July 2026

commitments.title: Amar Mahal-Trombay and Amar Mahal-Wadala-Parel water tunnels
commitments.committed_by: BMC (Rs ~940 cr, AMT-1 9.7 km + AMT-2 5.5 km)
commitments.what: The tunnels that re-plumb the island city's supply. AMT-1 targeted April 2026; connection works for both were done in a 30-hour shutdown on 5-6 May 2026.

commitment_source.label: FPJ (Aug 2024 target); Mumbai Press (May 2026 connection shutdown)

status_history.note: Physical connections completed in the May shutdown; full commissioning not yet publicly confirmed

commitments.title: Yewai-Kasheli-Mulund raw-water tunnels (14 + 21 km)
commitments.what: The next generation of raw-water conveyance from the dams; 6-7 year horizon from start of works.

commitment_source.label: BMC WSP RTI manual (Dec 2024); Newsband (works begun)

status_history.note: BMC 'has initiated work on a 21-kilometre water conveyance tunnel linking Yevai and Kasheli in Thane to Mulund' and will also build 'a 14-km tunnel from Yevai Reservoir to Kasheli', 'estimated to cost around Rs. 4,500 crore', in two phases. A civic official said the work order had been issued and construction was 'set to commence within the next month'; 'both tunnels are expected to be completed in six to seven years'. No progress figure is given.

For the 7.13 km Kasheli-Mulund tunnel, civic officials reported the 134-metre-deep launching shaft at Mulund completed and the 128-metre-deep recovery shaft at Kasheli excavated to 27 metres, with tunnel boring to begin by September; the tunnel is 'expected to be completed by October 2030'. We have not found a 2026 progress figure for the Yewai-Kasheli tunnel.
status_history.source_label: Free Press Journal, reporting civic officials after a site review by BMC's Additional Municipal Commissioner (Projects), 22 July 2026

commitments.title: Surya Phase-2: 218 MLD to Mira-Bhayandar
commitments.what: The pipeline that would close MBMC's documented gap (211 MLD sanctioned, ~195 received) and end its dependence on tanker-summer politics.

commitment_source.label: MMRDA WSRMC present status ('in progress'); allocation per the EC table

status_history.note: MMRDA's status page gave a 'Revised Date of Completion: 31.12.2025' and said 'The execution works of Phase-II are currently in progress. The works are planned for completion by end of Dec 2025.' Progress by component: Kashidkopar to Chene pipeline 87%, Chene MBR (for MBMC) 70%, Vasai Creek tunnel 25%, Kaman Creek tunnel 82%.
status_history.source_label: MMRDA WSRM Cell, Present Status page (Wayback Machine capture, 13 December 2025)

status_history.note: MMRDA's status page now gives a 'Revised Date of Completion: 31.12.2026' and says 'The works are now planned for completion by end of Dec 2026.' Progress by component: Kashidkopar to Chene pipeline 99% ('Balance length of 100 mts planned for completion by end of Aug 2026'), Chene MBR 100%, Vasai Creek tunnel 56% and Kaman Creek tunnel 82% (both planned for completion by end of Sept 2026). The page says commissioning of Phase-II depends on a 132 kV power supply from MSETCL. The new date has not passed.
status_history.source_label: MMRDA WSRM Cell, Present Status page (footer: 'Page last updated on : 17-10-2026'), read 18 October 2026

commitments.title: '403 of 496 flooding spots mitigated' - this monsoon adjudicates
commitments.what: BMC says 403 of the 496 listed spots are mitigated and 93 may face waterlogging in very heavy rain. The claim meets reality between June and September - and the list itself has grown 386 -> 453 -> 496 while mitigation was claimed at 80%+ each year.

commitment_source.label: Pre-monsoon briefing via HT/Curly Tales; trend via FPJ/Oneindia

status_history.note: At the Municipal Commissioner's first pre-monsoon media briefing: 'Mumbai has identified 496 areas where flooding can happen. Out of these, 403 spots have already been fixed', with 93 locations that may face waterlogging in very heavy rain.
status_history.source_label: Curly Tales, reporting the Municipal Commissioner's first pre-monsoon briefing, 29 April 2026

status_history.note: The monsoon window this row set (to September 2026) has passed. We have not found a BMC record of how the 403 spots described as mitigated performed, or of work completed at the remaining spots. In July the Municipal Commissioner said at a press conference that 'Waterlogging is unavoidable when around 300 mm of rain falls within a short span and coincides with a 4.5-metre high tide', and BMC was preparing a flood-mitigation project that 'aims to address 300-350 chronic flooding hotspots'. The outcome cannot be cited either way.
status_history.source_label: Free Press Journal, reporting the Municipal Commissioner's press conference, 7 July 2026

commitments.title: BRIMSTOWAD's last two pumping stations (Mogra, Mahul)
commitments.what: Six of the eight stormwater pumping stations recommended after the 2005 deluge are built (Haji Ali, Irla, Cleveland, Lovegrove, Britannia, Gazdarbund); Mogra and Mahul remain unbuilt two decades on - BMC's own ESR says so. Phase I stands at 19 of 20 works, Phase II at 26 of 38; Rs 2,541 crore spent, Rs 2,700 crore more needed (ESR, March 2025).

commitment_source.label: BMC ESR 2024-25, SWD chapter p.41 ('Mogra + Mahul pending'; spend + phase status)

status_history.note: Mogra tender finalised (Rs ~393 crore; ~24-month build)
Land amount deposited and preliminary work initiated; CZMA clearance obtained

The Mogra site was found to clash with Phase 2 of the Versova-Dahisar link road near Lokhandwala Creek Road - the station must shift westward and seek FRESH CRZ clearance. FPJ's framing: '19 years of delay'. Mahul has no equivalent movement

commitments.title: Mithi river widening and retaining walls - the last 6%
commitments.what: Widening 93.96% and walls 94.60% complete as of 30 April 2025 (BMC's own ESR) - two decades after the 2005 deluge made the Mithi the reference failure. The final stretches are the encroached, hardest ones.

status_history.note: BMC's ESR: 'As of now, the work of widening and deepening of the 17 Km long Mithi river is 93.96% completed and the work of constructing the protective wall is 94.60% completed'. The BMC stretch 'is almost complete, except for the section between the Kurla-Kalina Bridge and CST Bridge'. No completion date is given.

commitments.title: Kalu dam: 1,140 MLD for four cities - 'coming' since ~2010
commitments.what: The eastern corridor's designated future source (1,140 MLD for Thane, Bhiwandi, Kalyan-Dombivli, Ulhasnagar), built by KIDC as deposit work on MMRDA funds. MMRDA's own status page (through May 2026) still lists as pending: the forest-clearance NPV payment for 999.328 ha, acquisition of 1,259.54 ha of private land, and rehabilitation of 3,169 project-affected people.

commitment_source.label: MMRDA Kalu project page (official status through May 2026)

status_history.note: Bombay HC stayed the works on 2 March 2012 over missing forest clearances
Stay withdrawn 13 January 2020; KIDC recommenced land acquisition and rehabilitation. Rs 114.10 cr (dam) + Rs 396.44 cr (forest NPV) paid to KIDC through March 2023
Six years after the stay lifted, MMRDA's own page still lists forest NPV, 1,259.54 ha of land and 3,169 PAPs' rehabilitation as unresolved prerequisites

commitments.title: Bhiwandi +100 MLD augmentation (AMRUT 2.0)
commitments.what: The tendered augmentation that would nearly double Bhiwandi's ~94 MLD STEM quota - official acknowledgement that demand exceeds the paper.

commitment_source.label: Tender notice (Projects Today); FPJ Feb 2026 context

status_history.note: BNCMC 'has invited bids for augmentation to Bhiwandi-Nizampur water supply scheme of 100 MLD at Bhiwandi in Thane district of Maharashtra under AMRUT-2.0'; 'The estimated cost is Rs 328.99 crore, with a completion period of 24 months', and the last date for bids was 9 May 2023. No award or progress is recorded.
status_history.source_label: Projects Today, 28 March 2023 (Wayback Machine capture, 6 December 2025)

status_history.note: BNCMC's 2026-27 budget: 'Rs 25 crore has been earmarked for a 100 MLD water supply project under AMRUT 2.0.' The report gives no award, progress figure or completion date.
status_history.source_label: ThePrint (PTI), reporting the BNCMC budget for 2026-27, 25 March 2026

commitments.title: The climate budget's own scoreboard: 739 activities, 86.26% financial progress
commitments.what: India's first city climate budget publishes its own delivery claims annually - including flood-spot counts as a KPI. Each edition re-audits the last; the FY 2026-27 report, released in June 2026, re-audited FY 2025-26, and the next edition is the next checkpoint for this whole register's flood and reuse rows.

status_history.note: BMC's second Climate Budget Report: 'BMC achieved 86.26% financial progress' on its FY 2024-25 climate budget and 79.96% on the additional budget with MCAP components, 'with physical progress reported across 739 climate-linked budget activities'.
status_history.source_label: BMC, Climate Budget Report FY 2025-26 (released 5 June 2025; OpenCity copy)

status_history.note: The next edition re-audits FY 2025-26: BMC reports 77.91% financial progress on its FY 2025-26 climate budget (expenditure of Rs 12,654.54 crore as of 31 March 2026 against a revised estimate of Rs 16,242.75 crore) and 85.84% on the additional budget with MCAP components. Its physical-progress table counts 143 activities completed, nearing completion or on track, 195 ongoing with partial completion, 42 at tender stage, 60 token provisions and 19 cancelled.
status_history.source_label: BMC, Climate Budget Report FY 2026-27 (released 18 June 2026)

update_model: Statuses change only with a dated citation, and changes append to each commitment's history - the slippage trail is the product. The register re-verifies on a document calendar (pre-monsoon briefing in April, Praja in May, BMC ESR in June, the monsoon outcome in October, the Climate Budget in June, the MMRDA annual report) plus a due-date queue: when a promise's next_check passes, it enters the next verification sweep.
sources_note: Commitment sources are the institutions' own documents wherever they exist (Climate Budget commissioning table, ESR works chapters, NGT record, RTI manuals, MMRDA status pages); press citations are used for status changes the institutions have not yet published themselves.
